correctness.rationale: Fourier–Laurent diagonalization gives F(k)=M sigma3+[c sin(k)-ic(1-cos(k))] sigma1. For every support direction theta, the Hermitian symbol has eigenvalues plus/minus sqrt(M^2 cos^2(theta)+c^2(sin(k+theta)-sin(theta))^2). The exact maximum in k yields h(theta); optimizing the quadratic in |sin(theta)| yields both radius thresholds. Only theta=0,pi are support nonsmooth, giving exactly the two faces. A maximizer k set is finite for any theta, hence no supporting boundary is attained in L2. A checker independently sampled 2206 comparisons, but analytical arguments establish all infinite claims.

value.rationale: The recently introduced one-sided discrete Dirac operator has previously computed norm and spectral-radius transitions, but its numerical range controls nonnormal short-time growth and resolvent enclosures and had no evaluated geometry in inspected sources. The two different sharp mass transitions (outer plateau ends at sqrt(2)c, centered inradius reaches its plateau at sqrt(3)c), exact flat-face lengths, and nonattainment classify a natural full numerical-range invariant across all masses, not an arbitrary parameter slice. The exact formula may also benchmark numerical-range computations of lattice Dirac discretizations.
